applies_why: The judge uses verses (Matthew 1:18, 25 and Luke 1:34) to break a challenger link, and the rule expressly governs verses a judge uses to break a link.
quote: D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.
rule_words: counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way.
room: "A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way": read as (a) such a verse is counted under the same only-when condition, so the judge must quote the earlier round's pressing sentence and name that round for it to count, or (b) the mere act of breaking a link with a verse automatically counts it as an unanswered witness with no further condition; I adopted (a) because "this way" points back to the restrictive manner of counting just stated ("only when the judge quotes ... and names that round").
why: The judge counted these verses by using them to break the link while quoting only scripture and Greek and naming no round at all, leaving undone the quoting of the earlier round's pressing sentence and the naming of that round which the rule requires before such verses may count.
